### 1. 📱 Social Media Captions

**Platforms:** Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, X/Twitter, Facebook, YouTube (description)

**For every caption, produce:**
- Hook (first line — must work as a standalone sentence)
- Body (value, story, or proof — platform-appropriate length)
- CTA (one clear ask — varied, never repeated in a batch)
- Hashtags (3-5 for Instagram/TikTok, 3 max for LinkedIn, 1-2 for X)

**Caption vs. Script Rule — a caption paired with a video, Reel, or carousel never just retells it:**
When a caption accompanies content that already has its own words (a video voiceover, a Reel script, on-slide carousel copy), assume the viewer either just watched it or is about to. The caption's job is to summarize or complement that content, never to restate it line by line or paraphrase it beat by beat. Before delivering, check: could this caption have been produced by lightly rewording the script/slide copy? If yes, throw it out and rewrite from a genuinely different angle. Ways to complement instead of repeat:
- Zoom out to why it matters or who it's for, rather than what happens in it
- Add a detail, number, or context the video/carousel didn't include
- React to or frame the piece from outside it, as if introducing it to someone who hasn't seen it yet
- Speak directly to the viewer's own situation rather than narrating the creator's
The CTA and hashtags are unaffected by this rule — only the hook and body must stand apart from the underlying script or slide copy.

**Platform-specific rules:**
- **Instagram:** Hook + line breaks every 1-2 sentences + 3-5 hashtags. 150-300 words optimal for engagement posts. Shorter for Reel captions.
- **TikTok:** Shorter than Instagram. Hook is critical — first line determines if they click "more." 100-150 words max. 3-5 hashtags.
- **LinkedIn:** Hook must work before "see more" cut. Paragraphs over bullets. Personal story + professional insight formula. 150-300 words. 3 hashtags max. No external links in post body.
- **X/Twitter:** Lead tweet must stand alone. 280 char limit per tweet. If thread, each tweet = one idea.
- **Facebook:** Storytelling works. Longer captions acceptable. 150-400 words.
- **YouTube:** SEO-driven description. Hook sentence + keyword-rich summary + timestamps if applicable + CTA + links.

**Emoji Rules — tone-matched, never decorative:**

Emojis are punctuation with personality. Use them the way a real person would in a text or caption — to add warmth, emphasis, or energy that matches the moment. Never sprinkle them randomly. Never use them to perform emotion that isn't already in the words.

**How to use emojis correctly:**
- Match the emoji to the **client's voice and niche.** A personal injury lawyer uses 🙏 ⚖️ 💰 — not 🌸 ✨ 💅. A chef uses 🍽️ 🔥 👨‍🍳. A fitness coach uses 💪 🏃 🎯. Read the voice and match the energy.
- Place emojis **at the end of a line or sentence** — not mid-sentence where they break reading flow
- Use them to **replace or reinforce punctuation** — a 🙏 at the end of an emotional line lands harder than a period
- Use them to **signal a CTA** — 👇 for "in the comments below," 🔗 for "link in bio," 💬 for "DM me"
- **1-3 emojis max per caption** for professional/authority voices (lawyers, executives, consultants)
- **3-5 emojis** for lifestyle, food, wellness, and personal brand accounts
- **Never** use emojis in the hook line — they dilute the punch of the opening

**Emoji placement by content type:**
- End of a punchy statement that deserves emphasis: "She almost took $4,200. We got her $187,000. 💰"
- Before or after a CTA: "DM me HELP and let's talk. 👇" or "💬 DM HELP to get started."
- At the end of a community/emotional moment: "Drop a 🙏 if someone you know has been through this."
- In the middle of a list to break it visually — only if the list is 3+ items

**Never use these emojis generically:** ✨ 🌟 💫 🚀 🎉 unless the content is literally about those things or the client uses them naturally in their own voice. These are the AI emoji defaults — they signal template, not human.

**Batch mode:** When asked for multiple captions, vary:
- Hook style (insider reveal / specific number / mistake warning / direct address / origin story)
- CTA (never repeat the same CTA twice in a batch)
- Pillar (rotate across growth, trust, conversion content)
- Length (mix short punchy with longer storytelling)

## Platform Format Quick Reference

| Platform | Caption Length | Hashtags | Script Length | Key Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Instagram | 150-300w (feed) / 50-100w (Reel) | 3-5 | 15-90 sec | Hook in first line, line breaks |
| TikTok | 100-150w | 3-5 | 15-60 sec | Hook in first 1-2 sec |
| LinkedIn | 150-300w | 1-3 | 30-90 sec | Must work before "see more" |
| YouTube | 200-500w (description) | N/A | 5-20 min (long) / 15-60 sec (Short) | SEO keywords in description |
| X/Twitter | 280 char per tweet | 1-2 | 60 sec max | Lead tweet stands alone |
| Facebook | 150-400w | Optional | 30-90 sec | Storytelling works |
| Email | N/A | N/A | N/A | One CTA, curiosity subject line |
| Blog | 800-2000w | N/A | N/A | SEO + hook paragraph |

## Hook Style Library

Apply these across all content types. Never open two pieces in a batch with the same style.

| Style | Formula | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| **Insider Reveal** | "What [industry] doesn't want you to know about [topic]" | Education, rights, tips |
| **Specific Number** | "We went from [X] to [Y] in [timeframe]" | Proof, results, case studies |
| **Mistake Warning** | "If you've been doing [X], you may have already [consequence]" | Engagement bait, shares |
| **Direct Address** | "If you're a [specific person] in [specific situation], stop." | Conversion, targeted reach |
| **Origin Story** | "I [humble beginning]. Now [result]. Here's what changed." | Likeness, personal brand |
| **Bold Claim** | "[Surprising statement that demands proof]" | Viral potential, debate |
| **The Question** | "Why does [common thing] always [frustrating outcome]?" | Relatability, comments |

## CTA Rotation Library

Never repeat a CTA in a batch. Rotate through:

- Save this for later
- Share this with someone who needs it
- Comment [word] if you want [thing]
- Tag someone who [situation]
- DM [word] to [get something]
- Follow for more [topic]
- Drop a [emoji] if this hit different
- Tell me in the comments — [question]
- Link in bio for [thing]
- Reply to this email with [question or word]

### Framework 1: Viral Hooks
*Applied to: all opening lines — captions, Reel hooks, carousel Slide 1, email subject lines, blog H1, thread openers*

A hook has exactly ONE job: help the right viewer decide to keep watching. It must deliver two things:
1. **Topic clarity** — within 1-2 seconds, the viewer knows exactly what this is about
2. **On-target curiosity** — the viewer believes this is for THEM, and an open question pulls them forward

**The Four Hook Killers — diagnose and fix before any hook ships:**

**1. DELAY** — topic arrives too late. Delete everything before the topic. No greeting, no throat-clearing. The first noun phrase should carry the subject.
- ❌ "Okay so this is honestly one of the craziest things I've ever seen..."
- ✅ "Your meal prep is why you're ordering takeout by Thursday."

**2. CONFUSION** — the viewer has to re-read. Fewer words. Simpler words (6th-grade level). Active voice. One idea per sentence.
- ❌ "The reason consistency with your nutrition tends to break down is that the systems..."
- ✅ "You prep every Sunday. By Wednesday it falls apart. The reason isn't discipline."

**3. IRRELEVANCE** — clear, but not for ME. Swap me/my → you/your. Frame around a pain the viewer already feels.
- ❌ "I've struggled with consistency my whole life."
- ✅ "If you've restarted the same routine five times this year, this is the reason."

**4. DISINTEREST** — clear, relevant, still skippable. No contrast = no curiosity. Name the A (common belief) and put B against it. The bigger the believable distance, the stronger the hook.
- ❌ "Here are tips for better meal prep."
- ✅ "The most consistent clients I've ever had don't use a meal plan at all."

**Platform hook deadlines:**
- Reel/TikTok: ~2 seconds (spoken + visual)
- LinkedIn: first 1-2 lines before "...see more"
- Carousel: Slide 1, ≤9 words
- Newsletter: subject line earns the open; first line earns the read
- X/Twitter: first tweet must stand alone

**Banned openers (always flag):** "Let me explain" / "Story time:" without content / "Nobody talks about this" without naming the thing / A CTA as the opener / "Wait till you see this"

**Hook Checklist:**
- [ ] Topic clear in first 1-2 seconds? (no DELAY)
- [ ] Impossible to misunderstand on one pass? (no CONFUSION)
- [ ] You/your framing around a felt pain? (no IRRELEVANCE)
- [ ] A-vs-B contrast that opens a real question? (no DISINTEREST)
- [ ] Sounds like the client, not a template? (voice check)

### Framework 3: Dumbify
*Applied to: explainer Reels, educational carousels, how-to scripts, any piece that teaches something*

People don't churn because content is too simple. They churn because following it is **too much work.** Cut mental effort.

**Target:** ~8th-grade reading level for the body, ~6th for hooks. Simple language, not simple ideas — lower the reading level, not the thinking.

**The moves:**
1. **Cut jargon** — or swap for the word you'd use telling a friend who isn't in the field
2. **One idea per sentence** — break nested clauses into separate sentences
3. **Common words over fancy ones** — use not utilize, help not facilitate, show not demonstrate, about not approximately
4. **Concrete over abstract** — "the export button" not "the relevant control"; "you'll save 2 hours" not "efficiency gains"
5. **Active voice** — "the model picks the next word," not "the next word is selected by the model"
6. **Cut filler** — "basically," "in order to," "the fact that"
7. **Teach by example** — one concrete example lowers load more than a precise definition

**The 13-year-old test:** would a sharp 13-year-old follow it on the first pass? If no, simplify further. This doesn't mean the insight is for 13-year-olds — it means the words shouldn't require a law degree to follow.

**Don't overbake:** never flatten everything into short choppy sentences. Vary length — simplify the words and structure, not the rhythm. Don't remove technical terms an expert audience expects.

## Output Quality Standards

Every piece of content produced by this skill must pass this test before delivery:

- [ ] Opens with a hook that works as a standalone line
- [ ] One idea per section/slide/beat — never two combined
- [ ] Written in the client's voice — not generic marketing copy
- [ ] Platform-appropriate length and format
- [ ] CTA is specific, actionable, and not repeated in the batch
- [ ] No corporate language, no filler phrases ("In today's digital world...")
- [ ] Tied to a real outcome — growth, trust, or conversion
- [ ] Ready to copy-paste — zero placeholder brackets remaining
- [ ] Zero em dashes — replaced with periods, commas, colons, or restructured sentences
- [ ] Complete sentences throughout (fragments only in spoken scripts where cadence demands it)
- [ ] Emojis present in captions — tone-matched to client voice, 1-5 depending on brand, never in the hook line, never decorative defaults (✨🚀🌟)
- [ ] If this caption is paired with a video/Reel/carousel, it complements that content rather than restating it (see Caption vs. Script Rule above)

After delivering content, always close with:
> *"Which piece do you want to refine, or should I write the next batch?"*
